Our customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, and other notable agencies and companies domestically and internationally. We are currently seeking a Specialist Systems Engineer to join our team, focused on specifying requirements for propulsion systems. Candidates interested in applying for this position should have a background in systems engineering and an understanding of Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). This role demands meticulous attention to detail and the ability to manage projects under general supervision. Key Responsibilities: In this role, the Lead Systems Engineer will be expected to: Demonstrate comprehensive experience with planning, coordinating, implementing, and communicating Systems Engineering (SE) objectives and goals to all levels of leadership ensuring successful design, development and integration of rocket and liquid propulsion systems. Provide guidance, coaching and training to other employees across the company within Systems Engineering and SE&I. Demonstrate subject matter expertise within Systems Engineering that includes: requirements and functional analysis, risk management, and product development for liquid rocket and propulsion systems. Lead large cross functional teams or technical support staff to implement performance of assigned projects leading to Milestone reviews. Develop contract proposals, basis of estimates, and other SE artifacts to support the capture of new business. Recommend significant improvements to existing processes, new products, processes, policies, standards or operating plans in support of Systems Engineering and Integration. Apply advanced Systems Engineering techniques, including Model Based Systems Engineering methodologies, in the management of complex projects of strategic importance. Communicate results in oral presentations and written communication. Represent the organization in meetings/teleconferences to resolve important questions and to plan and coordinate work. Essential Job Functions: Requirement Development (60%): Develops systems, subsystem, and component requirements for rocket propulsion systems’ product development. Responsible for derivation, allocation, and documentation of requirements in requirements databases and specifications. Coordinates requirements and related specification change management with IPT members. Defines and coordinates requirements verification plans with integrated product team members, plans and manages compliance assessment and certification. These activities will be performed utilizing model-based systems engineering tools. Functional Analysis (15%): Performs functional analysis and coordinates system trade studies. Assembly will be on piece parts into completed sub-assembly using typical assembly tools, but could also include final assemblies, quality testing, re-work, etc. In our Redmond, WA, site (Seattle area), we fabricate, assemble, and test chemical and electric thrusters, as well as small scale propulsion systems. Work with management, supervision or lead personnel to prioritize work and meet critical deadlines. Provide rapid support while following proper housekeeping and safety procedures. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications: Requires a High School Diploma or equivalent and a minimum of 4 years of prior relevant experience or 2 years post-Secondary/Associates Degree with 0-2 years of prior related experience. Preferred Additional Skills: Understanding of electrical test equipment (DMM, oscilloscope, etc.). Knowledge of strippers, crimpers and installing solder splices. Certification to IPC 620 preferred. Familiarity with 5S and lean procedures. Ability and willingness to work other shifts and overtime as necessary. Oracle and Delmia experience. Knowledge of Laminar Flow environments and FOE/FOD controls a plus. Knowledge of mechanical assembly and test of electromechanical components. Strong foundation in electromagnetics, RF/microwave theory, and electronic warfare. Ability to work independently and as part of a multi-disciplinary team in the development of RF systems and assemblies. Experience designing RF products from UHF through E-band, including frequency synthesizers, up/down converters, front-end electronics, antenna tracking electronics, and complete RF systems. Experience with Cadence AWR/Microwave Office, PathWave RF Synthesis (Genesys), and Siemens EDA (Mentor Graphics) or similar tools. Understanding of noise figure, noise temperature, Eb/No, BER, receiver sensitivity, temperature effects, impedance interfaces, and isolation requirements. From long-range covert surveillance missions to search and rescue operations, our MX-series systems, and the mission systems solutions they are part of, produce stabilized high-magnification electro-optical and infrared images from airborne, marine and ground based platforms, enabling our customers to see first and act first. About the Role We are a team full of bright and exceptionally friendly people who work together to create a wide variety of solutions to complex and challenging problems. In order to ensure exceptional results, our team creates reusable IP by following a rigorous process that begins with requirements, is supported by documentation and ends with verification. Are you tired of critical customer bugs causing you to work every weekend? If so, you may be ready to trade some of your frustration for a process that has been proven to produce nearly perfect designs. Our team follows a standardized work flow and an efficient process that enables us to consistently create robust and reliable designs that our customers can rely upon. We focus our energy on future solutions, not fixing past mistakes. Our team is split into two equally valuable groups. The Design team owns the design and is responsible for creating innovative solutions for our customers. The Verification team is committed to confirming that the modules we produce behave exactly as specified. Neither group could stand on its own, but together are successful. Our team of highly skilled individuals have both a depth and breadth in their roles. We all perform some level of verification; we all participate in requirements definition & design engineering and we all take an active role in developing new design concepts and product launches. An FPGA design cannot live in isolation and we collaborate regularly with other departments to ensure the best solution at the system level. This collaboration has earned us a reputation for producing high quality designs that are easy to integrate and actively supported. We track and report design progress so that our Leadership team can be well informed as they allocate resources. We also understand the complex world of FPGA designs as a marathon, not a sprint. We recognize that being excellent in life goes well beyond engineering and includes actively participating in our communities and spending time with friends and family. With this in mind, we set aggressive but achievable goals that allow us to feel challenged while maintaining a work life balance. In short, it is a great place to work! Primary Responsibilities You will join the FPGA Design team and actively participate in the new product introduction (NPI) design process by creating solutions using digital design techniques primarily in the context of FPGA technology. This includes: Creating FPGA designs using the VHDL language Simulating your designs using Questa Sim Utilizing Xilinx design tools for synthesis, implementation, debugging and timing closure Assisting the Verification Team as required Integrating library modules within a larger FPGA design Verifying, Testing and debugging in hardware Participating in regular design reviews Presenting FPGA status updates at regular NPI project meetings Supporting product sustaining operations Generating high quality documentation Following departmental practices and coding guidelines Providing input and support to others outside of the FPGA team Contributing to the team’s knowledge by sharing lessons learned Participate in company educational events and training as needed Propose ideas for, and participate in, continuous inter and intra-group innovation Complete other tasks as assigned by Manager We are specifically looking for someone who is: Passionate about being excellent, yet humble enough to learn from others A collaborator, knowing that it improves the results of independent work Excited to follow a workflow and process that will produce high quality designs Required Education and Experiences Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical or Computer Engineering, or equivalent and minimum 6 years of prior relevant experience, or Graduate Degree and a minimum of 4 years of prior relevant experience, or In lieu of a degree, minimum of 10 years of prior relevant experience. Job Title – Head of Finance Job Location – Bristol, UK Job ID – 37829 About this opportunity and L3Harris UK Operating at 11 sites in the United Kingdom, L3Harris supports Britain's mission to secure and strengthen the country by delivering sovereign innovation across the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains. L3Harris’ Bristol location is the Headquarters for our Maritime UK business – a leading global supplier of integrated marine control systems and simulation products for warships, submarines and high-end commercial marine vessels worldwide. Since its inception, L3Harris has continuously iterated upon our Integrated Platform Management System (IPMS) technology and successfully exported and delivered the system to over 300 vessels across 27 navies worldwide. We have additional Maritime UK sites in Burgess Hill, Barrow-In-Furness and Portchester. Together, we are powering the Royal Navy’s adoption of autonomous surface vehicle technology as well as delivering autonomous capability to UK ports, harbours and offshore energy service providers. We are seeking a Head of Finance to lead a team of 11 people and have overall responsibility for all financial matters in the UK for L3Harris' Maritime division. A few of our employee benefits are: Hybrid working where possible, three days onsite per week Early finish on a Friday 25 days holiday per year (plus bank holidays), increasing with long service and with the opportunity to buy/sell up to 5 days Private medical insurance with optional family cover Pension scheme of up to 8% employer contribution Life Assurance 4x salary (flexible up to 10x) Group income protection Flexible opt-in extras such as a health care cash plan, dental insurance, gym membership, critical illness cover, cycle to work scheme, travel insurance and electric car scheme Employee Family Assistance Program providing mental health and wellbeing support Professional membership reimbursement What the role will involve The responsibilities of your role will include the following: Set up accounting systems and ensure accounting records are maintained compliant with UK Companies Act and UK GAAP Prepare monthly management accounts, forecasts and annual budget. Assist the local General Manager with monthly management reports on L3Harris' Maritime UK business performance, clearly identifying variances from plan. Preparation of annual statutory financial statements and necessary supporting information to ensure a timely clean audit by the companies’ external auditors. Cash management of L3Harris' Maritime UK business bank accounts and preparation of cash flow forecasts as required. Assistance with the preparation of bid proposals for contract changes and new opportunities and review subcontractor pricing submissions. Prepare and introduce best practice accounting policies and procedures for all L3Harris' Maritime UK business accounting matters. Ensure sound financial controls are established and rigorously followed. Responsible for all UK tax matters (including Corporation tax and VAT) Responsible for maintaining accounts and records in alignment with projects and other accounting functions. Review & finalisation of management accounts. Maintain accounting systems: Journal entries, general ledger, accounts receivables, accounts payable, revenue reconciliation, etc. Compiles data, allocates costs, and prepares reports on labour, equipment, depreciation and other operating expenses and analyses financial reporting requirements. Ensure all monthly, quarterly & annual corporate reporting deadlines are met. Achieve and demonstrate satisfactory compliance with corporate’s "Compliance Plan for Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICFR)" relating to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. Ensure that all corporate deadlines for testing and other requirements are met. What you’ll bring The role requires the following experience and skills: Professional Accounting Qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA) Degree qualified in a relevant Finance domain, unless qualified by work experience Industry experience in Defence, Aerospace, Maritime or relevant domain Knowledge of SAP essential; involvement in an implementation would be highly desirable. Leadership experience, managing a team of other finance professionals Experience of P&L management and managing financial process end-to-end for FP&A, budgeting, accounting. Other Finance systems such as Sage, HFM is desirable but not essential Important to know Due to the nature of our work many our roles require a UK nationality and the ability to obtain a security clearance. Job Title:Sr Analyst, MES Solutions Architect Job Code: 37817 Job Location: Melbourne, FL; Rochester, NY; Salt Lake City, UT Job Schedule: 9/80: Employees work 9 out of every 14 days – totaling 80 hours worked – and have every other Friday off Job Description: We are seeking a detail-oriented MES Solutions Architect to lead the functional architecture, optimization, and support of our multi-platform Manufacturing Execution System (MES) landscape. The role supports Aegis FactoryLogix (FLx), Eyelit MES, iBase-t Solumina, and the custom Zeus web application across multiple manufacturing sites. This position serves as the key bridge between manufacturing operations, other company sites, and IT, focusing on process excellence, system standardization, low-code configuration, and seamless integration with ERP/PLM systems. The successful candidate will provide both strategic architectural guidance and hands-on functional support, including dedicated support in restricted/closed secure manufacturing areas. Essential Functions: MES Architecture & Standardization: Design, optimize, and govern functional architecture across the heterogeneous MES portfolio (FactoryLogix, Eyelit, Solumina, and Zeus) to ensure consistency, scalability, and best-practice alignment. Process Optimization & Solution Design: Analyze manufacturing processes, identify inefficiencies, and architect enhancements in MES functionality related to production tracking, quality management, advanced planning & scheduling (APS), WIP visibility, and real-time data flow. Multi-Site Implementation & Rollout: Lead or support multi-site MES standardization initiatives, best-practice sharing, and new deployments (with specific focus on iBase-t Solumina implementations in closed secure areas). Integration & IT Collaboration: Partner with IT to define integration requirements with ERP and PLM systems, coordinate system updates, testing, and enhancements while ensuring business requirements are accurately translated into technical solutions. Secure Area Support: Provide dedicated MES support in restricted/closed secure manufacturing areas, including compliance with security protocols, access management, and ensuring system availability in controlled environments. To support/assist in the iBase-t Solumina MES deployments in the closed areas. Functional Support & User Enablement: Act as the primary functional expert and point of contact for end-users; provide advanced training, troubleshooting, and guidance on MES workflows and capabilities. Data Analysis & Continuous Improvement: Develop and analyze key performance reports (throughput, WIP, quality metrics) to drive root-cause analysis, performance monitoring, and digital transformation initiatives. Change Management & Documentation: Lead change-management activities for new MES functionality, configurations, and process changes; author and maintain detailed functional specifications, process flows, test scenarios, and user-acceptance documentation. Compliance & Governance: Ensure all MES solutions meet regulatory, quality, security, and traceability requirements in a highly regulated manufacturing environment. Stakeholder Collaboration: Build strong relationships with internal manufacturing teams, cross-functional partners, and external vendors to align MES solutions with evolving business needs. Qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree and minimum 6 years of prior relevant experience. Graduate Degree and a minimum of 4 years of prior related experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 10 years of prior related experience. 3+ years of experience as a Business Analyst, MES Analyst, or in a similar functional support role in a manufacturing environment. Preferred Additional Skills: Demonstrated hands-on experience with at least two of the following platforms (or comparable MES systems): Aegis FactoryLogix, Eyelit MES, iBase-t Solumina. Experience with custom web-based MES applications is a plus. Background in semiconductor, electronics, aerospace, or similar regulated manufacturing industries is a plus. Knowledge and experience with interfacing MES to ERP and PLM applications. Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to analyze complex business requirements and translate them into effective manufacturing execution solutions. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Requires basic knowledge of alloy type and material defect characteristics. Requires basic computer skills and the ability to navigate through manufacturing and quality systems. Industrial radiography radiation safety personnel (IRRSP) certification preferred Prior experience in the Aerospace industry is a plus. Level III Certification in digital radiography Work Environment and Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to use hands to finger, handle or feel.
